C-d = YES BY RULE 4, AND THE ROW IS A GOOD ILLUSTRATION OF WHY RULE 4 EXISTS. Table II's MTD Strategy row contains four arms and three of the four comparisons among them run in the direction the rubric declines: Topology-only against Aggregation-only against both varies the DOWNSTREAM action while the reputation stage is fixed, which is the CrowdGuard Table V and G2uardFL Table 10 shape. The one admissible comparison is Reactive T&A against Proactive T&A: the downstream pair of actions is nominally identical and what changes is the upstream trigger. It is imperfect -- proactive mode also alters the reconnection target, "Connect with benign nodes (reactive) or nodeswith higher reputation score (proactive)" (Fig. 2), so the downstream is not held perfectly fixed -- and rule 4 is explicit that an experiment PLAUSIBLY holding a downstream mechanism fixed while varying an upstream stage is coded YES even if imperfect. Recorded here so a reader can re-adjudicate: on a strict reading with no benefit of the doubt this row is C-d = NO, and the frame would then have a third primary. That is exactly the sensitivity the pre-registration's rule 4 was written to make visible rather than to hide, and A5 must report this row as the one whose C-d code rule 4 alone decides.

C-b IS THE BORDERLINE CODE AND IT DOES NOT AFFECT PRIMARY STATUS. Two readings are available. Under the first, C-a's pairing is reputation-detection with the MTD module, and NO reason for pairing those two is given anywhere -- a targeted grep for MTD or moving-target within 80 characters of a motivation verb returns ZERO hits, so the paper never says why moving the target should be combined with detecting the attacker. Under the second, the pairing whose reason is quoted is similarity-based detection with validation-loss-based detection, which Algorithm 1 conjoins in a single accept test and which the paper's own §II treats as distinct defense families; that reason is stated and is a constituent-insufficiency reason, so C-b = YES. I coded the second reading because the quotation requirement is satisfied for a real pairing of two defense criteria applied jointly in the same round. Rule 3, which resolves two-reading quotations against the paper being outcome-gated, does not discriminate here: C-d = YES, so PRIMARY = NO under both readings, and C-b affects only the DESIGN rate.

NOTE ON WHY THIS IS NOT THE FedZZ / MASA READING. In FedZZ the calibrator existed to produce the zones its one filter consumed, and in MASA the fusion existed to make the unlearning detector work in non-IID; in both, C-a coded NO on one mechanism realized in stages. Here the dynamic aggregation strategy is not machinery serving the reputation system -- it periodically switches among independently published robust aggregators and the paper states its purpose as enhancing robustness in its own right. A system can therefore reject every model the reputation stage flags AND still be aggregating with Krum or Median that round. Two mechanisms, same round.

DATASET-LEVEL OBSERVATION WORTH THE SPACE: this is the second decentralized-FL paper in the batch (with WFAgg, 2409.17754) and both compose. The frame's DFL papers are not a separate literature with different habits; they compose defenses for the same reasons the centralized ones do.
